question: Compare the historical CLOUD definition with the available modern cloud definition. Answer in three short sentences: paraphrase the two definitions, then say whether the old source settles the causal direction between electricity and cloud formation. Cite the exact source IDs in square brackets, for example [bri-0059-891965a7ca3e:region-10:0]. Do not silently repair OCR or name a scientist.

result.answer: The old Britannica entry defines a cloud as "a collection of vapours suspended in the atmosphere" [bri-0059-891965a7ca3e:region-10:0], while the modern Wikipedia definition describes a cloud as "a visible mass of condensed droplets or frozen crystals suspended in the atmosphere" [wiki-593754-1320064819-5941026ced18]. The old source explicitly states that whether clouds are formed by electricity or become electrified after formation "has not yet, as far as we know, been ascertained" and remains unresolved [bri-0059-891965a7ca3e:region-14:0].
